title: 2026 international maritime gaming and carbon-leakage QA

sources.title: UK ETS international maritime voyages consultation - accessible webpage
UK ETS scope expansion: maritime sector

facts.source_fact: Earlier consultation responses cited avoiding carbon leakage and loopholes as reasons to support international maritime coverage.
The consultation cites limited evidence of route changes to avoid EU ETS coverage.
It also cites some evidence of additional UK port calls being used to avoid full intra-European coverage.
The Authority states that 50% UK ETS coverage of international voyage emissions could reduce that incentive.
Reducing that incentive is presented as a way to reduce gaming and carbon-leakage risk.
The consultation notes this could potentially reduce UK port activity.
The consultation notes ETS maritime costs may be passed through using operator surcharges.
The extent of cost pass-through to final goods prices is described as uncertain.
The consultation asks whether action is needed against gaming, transhipment or evasion.
No specific anti-gaming measure is made final by this consultation.
